assessment.rationale: This simulation is strongly about layer composition and preserving higher-layer promises over UDP-feed, but it does not specify CAS object type-binding behavior. It therefore helps on boundary clarity and audit framing, yet fits this unknown-typed-object bakeoff only weakly because the needed opaque unknown-codec behavior is left to an unspecified upper layer.
strengths: Explicit concern for preserving higher-layer promises through binding.
Audit-oriented composition evidence is part of the design intent.
weaknesses: Does not directly define behavior for unknown CAS object codecs.
Leaves the decisive object-handling semantics to an unspecified higher layer.
Provides little concrete failure behavior for store/advertise/forward under unknown type pressure.
risks: An unspecified upper layer may hide unsafe parsing assumptions instead of proving opaque handling.
Transport-layer success could be mistaken for object-type conformance without explicit unknown-type promises.
Mixed-version durability is underdefined because unknown codec behavior is not bound in the specimen itself.
open_questions: What higher-layer protocol riding over UDP-feed would explicitly promise opaque handling for unknown CAS object codecs?
Can the composition proof show that a relay stores and forwards a CID without attempting unsafe parse or semantic validation?
What local audit record would distinguish opaque forwarding success from refusal or drop when the object type is unknown?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
